conditions.source:
The City Council convened to discuss the adoption of a resolution authorizing the City Manager to accept surplus federal property from the Department of the Navy. This action implements the Economic Development Conveyance Agreement for the former Naval Air Station Alameda, specifically focusing on Phase Two of the Alameda Point conveyance.

Jennifer Short, Chief Operating Officer, presented the details of the transfer, which includes 183 acres of land divided into 11 parcels. The division into multiple parcels is designed to isolate unique environmental conditions, ensuring clear legal descriptions and minimizing uncertainty for future development. The conveyance package includes deeds, covenants restricting property use due to pre-existing contamination, bills of sale for storm drain and sewer systems, and amendments to the master lease to account for buildings now owned by the city. The property consists of 37 acres of uplands and 146 acres of submerged property, primarily the seaplane lagoon.

Council members addressed liability concerns regarding environmental remediation. It was confirmed that the Navy retains perpetual liability for unforeseen environmental conditions under Superfund law. In cases of disputed causation for later-discovered contamination, the burden of proof falls on the new owner. To mitigate risk, the city has procured insurance, and developers are required to obtain pollution liability insurance, creating multiple layers of protection.

The council noted that Phase Two is a critical step in fulfilling obligations under the disposition development agreement with site developers, allowing the city to convey land to them. The timeline targets a March conveyance ceremony, an April public trust exchange, and the start of city construction later in 2017. Council members expressed strong support for the project, highlighting its significance in converting the site to civilian use and commending staff for their efforts.

The council unanimously approved the resolution authorizing the City Manager to accept the property and execute the necessary conveyance documents. Following this item, the meeting transitioned to a discussion on a proposed rent stabilization and tenant protection ordinance, with staff preparing to present on the matter after a short break.
